tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore
tools.description: PRIMARY TOOL — call FIRST for almost any question OR before an edit: how does X work, architecture, a bug, where/what is X, surveying an area, or the symbols you are about to change. Returns the verbatim source of the relevant symbols grouped by file in ONE capped call (Read-equivalent — treat the shown source as already Read; do NOT re-open those files), plus the call path among them. Query can be a natural-language question OR a bag of symbol/file names. Usually the ONLY call you need — more accurate context, in far fewer tokens and round-trips than a search/Read/Grep loop.

Returns the verbatim source of the relevant symbols grouped by file in ONE capped call (Read-equivalent — treat the shown source as already Read; do NOT re-open those files), plus the call path among them. query.description: Symbol names, file names, or short code terms to explore (e.g., "AuthService loginUser session-manager", "GraphTraverser BFS impact traversal.ts"). For a flow question, name the symbols spanning the flow (e.g. "mutateElement renderScene"). A natural-language question works too — no prior codegraph_search needed.

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to include source code from (default: 12)

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project to query (or any directory inside it) — codegraph uses the nearest .codegraph/ index at or above that path. Omit to use this session's default project. Pass it to query a second codebase, or when the server root has no index of its own (e.g. a monorepo where only sub-projects are indexed, so there is no default project).

# cpp-v1: C++ language slice evidence

The C++ slice (`oxide-cpp-v1`, [../../cpp.md](../../cpp.md)) is judged against G++, which
binds every direct call the way the build does. `oracle/oracle.py` compiles each
translation unit with `g++ -O0 -fcallgraph-info` and reads every direct call: its file
and line, the callee's mangled name and the definition GCC kept (a callee's definition is
where a unit that defines it, per `nm`, places it). G++'s call column is not the call's
own (calls in another call's arguments carry that call's `(`, a temporary its `)`), so
each oxide `calls` edge is matched to the GCC callees of the same unqualified name
(`c++filt -p`) on the line of its `(`. A resolved edge agrees when its target is a
function or method whose source holds such a callee's definition line, for every such
callee a compiled unit defines (a template's call site binds once per instantiation;
"agree for some" is reported apart). A resolved prototype whose callee no compiled unit
defines there is checked against the declaration GCC kept. Edges to macros, which GCC
sees expanded, are counted and not judged. Measured with g++ 16.2.1.

Corpora (sources outside the repository, `~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/cpp-v1`), each
captured whole (tests, bundled gtest/gmock and docs included):
- yaml-cpp 0.8.0 (`yaml-cpp.tgz`, sha256 `fbe74bbd…3a16`): the 31 units of `src/` and
  `src/contrib/`, `-std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc`;
- fmt 11.1.4 (`fmt.tgz`, sha256 `ac366b7b…1e1e`): `src/format.cc`, `src/os.cc`, every
  `test/*-test.cc`, the test utilities and the bundled `gmock-gtest-all.cc`,
  `-std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint`
  (28 units; `format-impl-test.cc`, `header-only-test.cc` and `module-test.cc` do not
  compile with these flags and are skipped).

## Results (measured)

| Tally | yaml-cpp | fmt |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| G++ calls to a captured definition (in units / in headers) | 1,491 / 726 | 36,748 / 45,708 |
| resolved, agree | **640** | **2,244** |
| resolved, disagree | **0** | **7** |
| resolved, agree for some instantiations or overloads on the line | 8 | 1 |
| resolved, callee defined in no compiled unit | 0 | 15 |
| resolved to a macro / ambiguous to a macro, not judged | 7,950 / 81 | 2,883 / 420 |
| ambiguous, GCC binds a captured definition | 66 | 611 |
| unresolved, GCC binds a captured definition | 0 | 2,083 |
| unresolved, GCC binds an external one / one no unit compiles | 15 / 1 | 281 / 346 |
| no GCC call of that name on the line (resolved, ambiguous, unresolved) | 7,941 / 1,229 / 17,650 | 1,168 / 338 / 3,551 |

Precision on judged resolved edges is 1.0 on yaml-cpp and 0.997 on fmt. The 7 fmt
disagreements, characterized:
- 3 are `FMT_POSIX_CALL(dup(fd))`-style calls inside a class with a `dup` member: the
  macro makes them `::dup` (or the test build's `test::dup`); macro expansion is not
  modeled;
- 1 is argument-dependent lookup (`format_as(value)` binds a function in the argument
  type's namespace), not modeled;
- 1 is in the gtest amalgamation, where parse errors lost a namespace's nesting, so the
  call bound the header's prototype of the same function under another qualified name;
- 2 are templates: `formatter<string_view>::format(...)` drops its template argument, so
  it binds the enclosing `formatter<throws_on_move>` specialization's own `format`; and a
  `scan_data<…>()` constructor bound to another constructor of the same arity.

The "agree for some" cases are lines that call two overloads of one name (`RegEx(' ') |
RegEx("\r\n")`, gtest's `Message` copy and default constructors) or a template
instantiated so that its call binds differently; the oracle cannot separate them by line.
Recall is low by design: most G++ calls to captured definitions go through objects
(`x.f()`, `p->f()`) and need types, which the slice does not record (docs/cpp.md); "no
GCC call" edges sit in code no compiled unit instantiates or includes (templates, test
helpers, bundled gtest), or in macro arguments G++ reports elsewhere.

Every disagreement found while building the slice was traced and fixed or explained
before these numbers. Fixed in the slice: C's "every external definition" linkage rule
bound fmt's own `fprintf` template to libc calls in units that never declare it (C++
calls now need a visible declaration); default arguments on a prototype made its
out-of-line definition look too strict (arity is shared by declarations of the same
parameter count); and the unexpanded-macro idioms in docs/cpp.md, which had folded most
of `fmt/format.h` into one parse error. Fixed in the oracle: G++'s columns, unit-prefixed
internal symbols, and callees defined in units first left uncompiled.

The C slice's GCC oracle is unchanged by this slice: Lua 3,036 agree / 0 disagree,
hiredis in Redis 975 / 0 ([../c-v1](../c-v1/README.md)). Of Redis's 274 `.h` files, the two
Qt adapter headers (`deps/hiredis/adapters/qt.h`, `examples/example-qt.h`) are now C++;
Lua's 27 stay C.

Coverage and cost (measured, `derive` only, 200% CPU cap): fmt 69 C++ files, 44
complete and 25 partial, 1.3 s; yaml-cpp 246 C++ files (bundled gtest included), 183
complete and 63 partial, 2.1 s.

Not measured: retrieval or context quality on C++ tasks. ContextBench holds 60 C++
rows (fmt, nlohmann/json, simdjson, Catch2, ponyc, …), but no diagnostic was run; the
pinned baseline corpora hold no C++, and their baselines move by identity only
([../baseline-v17](../baseline-v17/README.md), [../typescript-v14](../typescript-v14/README.md)).

## Verification (Linux, measured)

Logs are in [verification/](verification/):
- `mise-verify.log`: ruff clean, mypy `--strict` clean (78 files), pytest 425 passed,
  7 skipped, `test_baseline.py` against baseline-v17 included.
- `distribution-wheel.log`, `distribution-sdist.log`: both artifacts install, index the
  fixtures (82 files, 403 entities) and pass `scripts/smoke_dist.py` (`exit=0`). The first
  run failed: the copied C++ fixture's two `Store::must_get` entities ranked above Rust's
  `<impl Store>.must_get`, which the Rust check required at rank 1; it now requires the
  Rust entity among the results (extraction unchanged). The TypeScript gate was not rerun
  for this slice.

## Reproduce

```
uv run python docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/oracle.py $YAML docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/yaml-cpp-oracle.json 'src/*.cpp' 'src/contrib/*.cpp' -- -std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc
uv run python docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/oracle.py $FMT docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/fmt-oracle.json 'src/format.cc' 'src/os.cc' 'test/*-test.cc' 'test/gtest-extra.cc' 'test/util.cc' 'test/test-main.cc' 'test/gtest/gmock-gtest-all.cc' -- -std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint
```

`*-oracle.json` lists every disagreement (with "agree for some"), every miss (`missed`)
and every resolved edge in a unit without a GCC call of its name (`unseen`);
`*-oracle.log` is the printed tally.

content.content:
- End-to-end deterministic offline context uses TreeIndex/TreeRouter/heuristic DecisionProvider/ContextPacker without any learned component, JEV, or inference runner. Optional JEV work does not block the deterministic phase exit.
- Entry-point retrieval, TreeIndex navigation, TreeRouter, graph, capsules, decisions, plan, expansion, and final bundle can be independently inspected/replayed.
- Capsule/dataset rendering agrees; no gold/final policy outcome enters model input.
- Graph membership is distinct from inclusion; expanded neighbors compete within the same budget and terminate under limits.
- Packer handles zero/tiny budgets, oversized entities, overlapping source, and unavailable prerequisites while satisfying the declared token budget and coherence rules.
- Required-symbol recall, labeled context noise, tokens, coherence and cost are measurable against no-expansion/heuristic/greedy controls.
- JEV disabled, failed, malformed, uncalibrated or abstaining leaves bounded heuristic routing/inclusion functional; captured provider responses replay deterministically even if the service itself is nondeterministic.

TreeIndex/TreeRouter are foundational concepts with open schema/algorithm decisions. TreeSelect, if retained as a name for an inclusion experiment, is separate from TreeRouter and remains unspecified until objective, TreeIndex view, prerequisites, complexity, and evaluation are documented. Greedy inclusion plus deterministic bounded routing is sufficient for the baseline; do not implement an unspecified optimizer.

### Phase 5 — Judge specialization, calibration and DecisionBench

Deliver:

- Optional local specialized judge and stronger-judge escalation experiments through the existing DecisionProvider/subject contract. The foundational interface, JEV capability planning and uncertainty/fallback have already been designed in earlier phases.
- Runtime provider-client orchestration and shared routing/candidate request limits, timeouts and explicit privacy/cost rules. External runners own inference execution; native execution needs separate benchmark justification.
- DecisionBench record/provenance/split design aligned to runtime candidate/branch capsules; realistic entry-point/routed/branch hard negatives, teacher uncertainty/audit, visitation-bias controls, and repository-held-out calibration/test procedures. Sentence Transformers may be a research/reference tool.
- Separate branch/candidate evaluation for discrimination, validity/repeatability, calibration, risk-coverage, position bias, fallback/routing, and end-to-end request/runner cost; preserve no-model and heuristic controls. Existing JEV validity failure is not evidence of either quality gain or quality rejection.

Exit gate:

- Disabled, failed, malformed, uncertain, or unavailable learned inference all leave deterministic context construction functional and observable.
- Models cannot alter traversal rules, thresholds, expansion, hard inclusion, budget, or fallback. Judgments remain separate from entry-point scores and TreeRouter/inclusion/packing policy outcomes; no judge is treated as a code-correctness reasoner.
- Dataset records use the same input semantics/renderer as inference, and policy decisions are not mislabeled as ground-truth relevance.
- No learned model is promoted without a frozen repository-held-out quality/calibration/cost protocol. A trained checkpoint is not required to complete this architectural interface phase.

### Phase 6 — Python migration (ADR-0011)

Replace the Rust kernel/runtime and Bun control plane with one Python package, without new retrieval experiments or model training.

Delivered (2026-10-15):

- `oxide` package (`src/oxide/`), uv-managed; `mise run verify` runs Ruff (lint, format), mypy `--strict` and pytest.
- Vertical slice over persisted state: `index_repository` → `search` → `build_context`, typed results, CLI (`oxide index|search|context|prepare`).
- Python language slice with the Rust `oxide-python-v1` semantics, one tree-sitter query; capture with `.gitignore`, skips and consistency retry; LadybugDB generations with lock, atomic publication, read-back and digest-verified hydration.
- Retrieval and TreeRouter reproduce `docs/phase-3/baseline-v1` exactly on all 7 tasks (test oracle). Context reaches Phase 4 config B's required-symbol recall 1.0 at 1,024 units.
- Tests for parsing/indexing, graph relations, retrieval, budgets/provenance, persistence/recovery/ownership, errors, CLI subprocesses and data isolation (every test and subprocess gets a private data location).
- Rust/Bun production code removed; recoverable at `f79808a`.

Exit gates for the migration:

1. Every public operation the Rust/TS stack offered or planned has a Python equivalent or a recorded decision not to port it (ADR-0011 § What was removed).
2. Retrieval and routing reproduce the frozen Phase 3 baseline; context quality is no worse than the Phase 4 heuristic baseline on its fixture.
3. `mise run verify` passes from a clean checkout after `mise run bootstrap` (FTS extension and, since the quality gate, the ContextBench corpora).

Delivered (2026-10-16): `oxide mcp`, a stateless FastMCP server over `oxide.api` (`oxide_search`, `oxide_context`; stdio, and stateless Streamable HTTP on loopback), opening the repository per call and tested with FastMCP's client in memory, over stdio and over HTTP with private data locations (`docs/public-api.md` § MCP).

Delivered (2026-10-16): the context-quality regression gate. `tests/python/contextbench.py` evaluates entry-point recall/MRR, routed coverage, packed recall, utilization and loss diagnostics at 256/1,024/4,096 units on 7 fixture and 37 ContextBench Python tasks (human gold, dev/held-out split by repository); `docs/phase-6/baseline-v1/` freezes the protocol, tasks, per-task results and manifest, and `test_contextbench.py` gates quality and output compatibility separately in `mise run verify`. Read-only MCP and CLI requests no longer create empty stores (`open_repository(..., create=False)`).

Delivered (2026-10-16): ContextBench scorer v2 and gold audit (`docs/phase-6/baseline-v2/`). Every annotated span is checked against its own content at the pinned commit: 176 of 208 verify (2 after a recorded path correction), 32 are reported separately as unverified with their class (annotation range errors, patched-revision content, drift, empty). Gold lines exclude blank lines, module-level gold is coverable through file entities, and every lost span is attributed to entry, routing, unsupported evidence, selection or budget. The engine output is unchanged.

Delivered (2026-10-16): module-level evidence in ContextPacker (`oxide-select-greedy-v3`, `oxide-payload-v3`, `docs/phase-6/baseline-v3/`). A parsed Python file retrieved by lexical match or hint packs its module-level source (imports, constants, top-level statements) as bounded runs between its top-level declarations, with a first-run header view and explicit omissions; files reached only by routing stay containers.

Closed (2026-10-16): the selection R&D iteration. Its last experiment, letting routed-only files pack module-level evidence, was INCONCLUSIVE at the preregistered dev-coverage check (one dev task; `docs/phase-6/routed-module-selection/`); `oxide-select-greedy-v3` stays the default.

Delivered (2026-10-17): incremental indexing and indexing UX (`docs/phase-6/incremental-indexing/`). Each generation seals the parse facts of its Python files (`facts.json`, digest in the manifest); `index()` reuses them for unchanged bytes while resolution and publication stay whole-snapshot, so the result equals a full rebuild (parity tested over cross-file edits, moves, deletions and damaged facts). On 3,539 files an edit re-index drops from ~14.5 s to ~9.8 s; cold builds cost ~9% more. `IndexReport` names added/modified/deleted paths and parsed/reused counts; `oxide index` prints stage progress and a change summary.

Delivered (2026-10-17): the TypeScript language slice (`oxide-typescript-v1`, [docs/typescript.md](typescript.md)). `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts`/`.d.ts` and `.tsx` files are parsed by pinned `tree-sitter-typescript` grammars into the same entities and relations as Python: declarations of every kind with ADR-0010 identities (overload ordinals, `<default>`/`<module>` synthetic names), `module:typescript:` modules, ES-module resolution of relative specifiers through named, default, namespace and `export *` re-exports, lexical-scope calls including JSX components, heritage references and Jest/Vitest `tested_by`. Unknowable names stay unresolved. Parse facts are cached per dialect (`oxide-facts-v2`), so incremental indexing equals a full rebuild for both languages. Python output is unchanged; `docs/phase-6/baseline-v4/` re-freezes v3 for the new derivation id only.

Delivered (2026-10-17): the TypeScript context-quality baseline (`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, `contextbench-ts-v1`). `tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` applies the ContextBench-py ruler to 8 fixture and 81 ContextBench TypeScript tasks (mui, vue held out; vscode, code-server, darkreader dev), with a gold audit (two annotation defects handled: absolute paths, `cat -n` content), grammar-derived module lines validated against OXIDE on 7,353 files, and a structural cause for every span lost before packing (router bound, unresolved import by a path oracle, partial parse, no path). Verified `span_recall@4096` is 0.244 and 70% of verified spans are lost at entry; of pre-packing losses, 54% have no structural path, 24% sit behind unresolved `baseUrl`/workspace imports, 22% behind router bounds. No vscode corpus indexes with the default 128 MiB buffer pool. Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate is `mise run contextbench-ts`.

Delivered (2026-10-17): large-repository reliability and TypeScript module resolution (`docs/phase-6/typescript-v2/`, `contextbench-ts-v2`). The LadybugDB load pool is `BUFFER_POOL` plus twice the CSV bytes a load copies ([docs/large-repositories.md](large-repositories.md)): all 14 VS Code corpora index with the default settings (v1: 0 of 14), with results identical to v1 and the same peak RSS as the old 512 MiB override. Bare specifiers resolve through the owning `tsconfig.json`'s `paths` and `baseUrl` (`oxide-typescript-v2`, `src/oxide/core/tsconfig.py`), with `extends`, `files`/`include`/`exclude` and TypeScript's lookup order; unknowable projects and package lookups stay unresolved. On the same corpora, VS Code's unresolved imports drop from 802k to 53k and spans behind unresolved imports from 71 to 22. They become router-bound (64 → 120), so no context-quality metric changes. Python is re-frozen as `baseline-v5` for the derivation id only.

Delivered (2026-10-17): explicit path hints that pay off (`oxide-select-greedy-v4`, `docs/phase-6/path-hint-utility/`, PROMOTE). Before, a correct `paths` hint reached the file but packed its module-level glue first and its declarations after every lexical hit elsewhere, so hinted `line_recall@4096` equaled unhinted. Now candidates in a hinted file are packed first, by the usual value and floor, and the hinted file contributes only its header view. Dev hinted `line_recall@4096` rises from 0.685 to 0.785 (py) and from 0.360 to 0.626 (ts); the one-time held-out confirmation gives 0.273 → 0.545 and 0.420 → 0.728. Unhinted output is byte-identical; ContextBench is re-frozen as `baseline-v6` and `typescript-v3` for the selector version only. This closes general retrieval R&D for this release.

Delivered (2026-10-18): one MCP tool and parser limits. `oxide mcp` serves exactly one tool, `oxide_search`, whose `mode` is `search` (the old `oxide_search`, same arguments and output) or `context` (the old `oxide_context`, byte-identical); `oxide_context` is removed (`docs/public-api.md` § MCP, migration). Structural search stays a Python API (`Repository.structural_search`, `oxide[structural]`): a preregistered agent trial (`docs/phase-6/structural-mcp-trial/`, REJECT) found agents with grep already at 0.978 shape-task F1 against 0.994 with structural mode, and they never called the search or context modes either. Both language slices now parse long method chains and deep nests in linear time (30k links: 29.6 s → 0.12 s) and refuse syntax deeper than tree-sitter's 16-bit query depth with an explicit diagnostic, where matches were silently dropped before (`docs/parser-limits.md`). The slice versions moved to `oxide-python-v3` and `oxide-typescript-v3`, re-frozen as `baseline-v8` and `typescript-v5` for the derivation id only.

Python output is unchanged; `docs/phase-6/baseline-v4/` re-freezes v3 for the new derivation id only.

Delivered (2026-10-17): the TypeScript context-quality baseline (`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, `contextbench-ts-v1`). `tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` applies the ContextBench-py ruler to 8 fixture and 81 ContextBench TypeScript tasks (mui, vue held out; vscode, code-server, darkreader dev), with a gold audit (two annotation defects handled: absolute paths, `cat -n` content), grammar-derived module lines validated against OXIDE on 7,353 files, and a structural cause for every span lost before packing (router bound, unresolved import by a path oracle, partial parse, no path). Verified `span_recall@4096` is 0.244 and 70% of verified spans are lost at entry; of pre-packing losses, 54% have no structural path, 24% sit behind unresolved `baseUrl`/workspace imports, 22% behind router bounds. No vscode corpus indexes with the default 128 MiB buffer pool. Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate is `mise run contextbench-ts`.

Delivered (2026-10-17): large-repository reliability and TypeScript module resolution (`docs/phase-6/typescript-v2/`, `contextbench-ts-v2`). The LadybugDB load pool is `BUFFER_POOL` plus twice the CSV bytes a load copies ([docs/large-repositories.md](large-repositories.md)): all 14 VS Code corpora index with the default settings (v1: 0 of 14), with results identical to v1 and the same peak RSS as the old 512 MiB override. Bare specifiers resolve through the owning `tsconfig.json`'s `paths` and `baseUrl` (`oxide-typescript-v2`, `src/oxide/core/tsconfig.py`), with `extends`, `files`/`include`/`exclude` and TypeScript's lookup order; unknowable projects and package lookups stay unresolved. On the same corpora, VS Code's unresolved imports drop from 802k to 53k and spans behind unresolved imports from 71 to 22. They become router-bound (64 → 120), so no context-quality metric changes. Python is re-frozen as `baseline-v5` for the derivation id only.

Delivered (2026-10-17): explicit path hints that pay off (`oxide-select-greedy-v4`, `docs/phase-6/path-hint-utility/`, PROMOTE). Before, a correct `paths` hint reached the file but packed its module-level glue first and its declarations after every lexical hit elsewhere, so hinted `line_recall@4096` equaled unhinted. Now candidates in a hinted file are packed first, by the usual value and floor, and the hinted file contributes only its header view. Dev hinted `line_recall@4096` rises from 0.685 to 0.785 (py) and from 0.360 to 0.626 (ts); the one-time held-out confirmation gives 0.273 → 0.545 and 0.420 → 0.728. Unhinted output is byte-identical; ContextBench is re-frozen as `baseline-v6` and `typescript-v3` for the selector version only. This closes general retrieval R&D for this release.

Delivered (2026-10-18): one MCP tool and parser limits. `oxide mcp` serves exactly one tool, `oxide_search`, whose `mode` is `search` (the old `oxide_search`, same arguments and output) or `context` (the old `oxide_context`, byte-identical); `oxide_context` is removed (`docs/public-api.md` § MCP, migration). Structural search stays a Python API (`Repository.structural_search`, `oxide[structural]`): a preregistered agent trial (`docs/phase-6/structural-mcp-trial/`, REJECT) found agents with grep already at 0.978 shape-task F1 against 0.994 with structural mode, and they never called the search or context modes either. Both language slices now parse long method chains and deep nests in linear time (30k links: 29.6 s → 0.12 s) and refuse syntax deeper than tree-sitter's 16-bit query depth with an explicit diagnostic, where matches were silently dropped before (`docs/parser-limits.md`). The slice versions moved to `oxide-python-v3` and `oxide-typescript-v3`, re-frozen as `baseline-v8` and `typescript-v5` for the derivation id only.

**Cleanup**
- **Deleted junk:** four empty logs in `docs/phase-6/rust-v1/real/`, an empty root file `md`, and a stray Python virtualenv folder `activate/`. None of them were tracked by git.
- **Fixed stale references:** `mise.toml` and `docs/agents/workflow.md` said the latest TypeScript baseline was `typescript-v8`. The code actually uses `typescript-v14`, so both now say that.

  - The security-audit skill and its entry in `skills-lock.json`.
  - The new Go-oracle section in the go-v1 docs.

**C++ verification**
- The C++ notes said the TypeScript quality gate hadn't been rerun for this slice. I ran it with the usual 200% CPU / 3 GB limits: 17 passed in 14 min against `typescript-v14`.
- The log is in `docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/verification/contextbench-ts.log`, and `docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/README.md` now records the result.

**Merge readiness**
- `main` has nothing `rewrite/v2` lacks, so the 144 commits merge as a fast-forward.
- CI and the Platforms run are both green on the current commit `64ee0de`.
- These migration exit gates are met; I didn't check the others:
  - Retrieval reproduces the frozen Phase 3 baseline (checked by the test suite).
  - `mise run verify` passes in CI.

**Needs your call before committing or merging**
1. **pyrefly:** `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` add a new dev dependency, `pyrefly`, but `mise run verify` never runs it. AGENTS.md asks for a stated reason for any new dependency. Should it be kept and documented, or dropped?

   - `.mcp.json`
   - `opencode.jsonc`
   - `.claude/CLAUDE.md`

I didn't run the C++ retrieval/context-quality check on the 60 C++ benchmark rows; its docs record it as not measured. I also didn't rerun the full `mise run verify` locally after these doc-only edits, and CI ran on the commit, not on this working tree.

Since 2026-10-05 all eval data (`oxide-jev-eval`, `oxide-capremoval-eval`, `oxide-tree-eval`, `oxide-treeselect-eval`, `oxide-typed-eval`, ~43 GB) lives in `~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/`; `~/.cache/<name>` are symlinks to it.

**Why:** user asked to keep run state somewhere persistent, not temp and not something cleared to save space.
**How to apply:** put new eval corpora and runs in a per-study subdirectory there (e.g. `oxide-go-eval/`); never delete that directory to free space. The ContextBench `full.parquet` (SHA-checked) is at `oxide-jev-eval/contextbench-full.parquet`. Older RESUME.md notes predate the vectorless Python engine. See [[tree-direction]].

`report.md` and `ripgrep-oracle.json` hold the first-pass output, and the classification
above was done by hand. The program and its outputs are in [oracle/](oracle/report.md).

## ContextBench diagnostic

Both arms used the same 22 rows from 9 repositories (`rust-rows.json`, SHA-256
`92f4a2cdab49cb6c53f5fe9021c35edfa3c212c00b1fe14d6f36e61c19551011`), the same corpora,
gold and scorer. Before ran b128a90 in an isolated environment; after ran this checkout.
Gold-audit classes were identical in both arms: 11 exact, 114 path-only, 13 unresolved
(138 spans); the unresolved class is excluded from verified metrics.

| Verified macro metric (22 tasks, 125 spans, 14,229 lines) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Entry recall@20 | 0.292767 | 0.323178 |
| Routed coverage | 0.304131 | 0.626804 |
| Complete span recall@1,024 | 0 | 0.005682 |
| Complete span recall@4,096 | 0 | 0.104167 |
| Line recall@4,096 | 0 | 0.096705 |

Median index time per task was 0.335 s before and 1.506 s after; peak process RSS was
154.3 MiB and 310.5 MiB. No parameters were tuned. This is a small diagnostic (n=22),
not a gate or broad quality claim. Raw scores, audits and timings are in
`context-before/` and `context-after/`; the run summary is
`verification/contextbench-rust.md`.

## Successor baselines, distribution and limitations

[`baseline-v11`](../baseline-v11/README.md) and
[`typescript-v8`](../typescript-v8/README.md) are identity-only successors for the
derivation identity change: metrics are byte-identical and only derivation/identity
fields changed (`verification/baselines.md`). Wheel and sdist smoke passed in fresh
virtual environments, including a Rust impl-method search and context check
(`verification/distribution-*.log`).

Unsupported constructs are listed under "Not modeled" in [../../rust.md](../../rust.md):
method calls on non-`self` receivers and trait dispatch, type-alias owners, enum-variant
glob imports, macro arguments/bodies and macro-defined items, `cfg` evaluation, and
registry/git dependencies. Windows and macOS Rust runtime and artifact checks remain
pending hosted CI; wheel availability does not establish runtime support. The platform
matrix and existing LadybugDB limits still apply.

Reproduce from a locked checkout, under the resource caps recorded in the evaluation
logs:

```sh
mise run verify
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_rust.py real /path/to/ripgrep docs/phase-6/rust-v1/real/ripgrep.json
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_rust.py audit /path/to/ripgrep docs/phase-6/rust-v1/real/ripgrep-audit.json
uv run --locked python scripts/bench.py /path/to/ripgrep --iterations 3 --warm 3 --query SearcherBuilder --query Matcher
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_rust.py rows /path/to/contextbench.parquet /path/to/rust-rows.json
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_rust.py fetch /path/to/rust-rows.json /path/to/corpora
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_rust.py context /path/to/rust-rows.json /path/to/corpora docs/phase-6/rust-v1/context-after
# rust-analyzer oracle: needs the 1.98.0 toolchain's rust-analyzer; paths are set at the top of the script
uv run --locked python docs/phase-6/rust-v1/oracle/run_oracle.py
```

The previous-engine ContextBench arm requires its recorded isolated environment and the
same rows and corpora. Distribution smoke follows [platforms.md](../../platforms.md).
Next language: Java or C#, chosen against a scoped fixture and a resolution oracle
(javac/JDT or Roslyn) before implementation, since both need the type-directed member
resolution that the Rust and Go slices leave unmodeled.

`class A` (which declares a member class `A.JsonAdapter`) resolved to the member class. javac resolves the
annotations of a class declaration in the enclosing scope, so the import wins. See
[Fix and re-measurement](#fix-and-re-measurement).

**First pass vs final.** The first scoring pass had one scorer error class: explicit type-argument calls
(`gson.<Car>fromJson`) were queried at the receiver, which made 8 ambiguous edges look like none-of-candidates.
After the fix, the precision numbers are unchanged and the ambiguous-in-none count drops from 8 to 0.

## ContextBench Java diagnostic (before/after)

Rows: [java-rows.json](java-rows.json), SHA-256 `4041983b1e94233a2425963fadd0abcd39f13c36a0401d03998309776bf65430`.
The fixed `select` rule picked 16 rows from 6 repositories:
- fastjson2 3, logstash 3, jackson-core 3, mockito 3;
- gson 2, jib 2.

All 16 were fetched (shallow `git archive` projections of `.java` and build files). Both arms used the same rows,
scorer and gold audit (`gold-audit.json` is byte-identical): 37 exact, 50 path and 10 unresolved spans. BEFORE is
the engine at `3492b38` in a worktree with its own venv (the worktree is now removed); AFTER is this checkout.
Macro metrics, verified gold (16 tasks, 87 spans):

| Arm | entry recall@20 | routed coverage | span recall@1,024 | span recall@4,096 | line recall@4,096 | file recall@4,096 | Median index | Peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| before | 0.2147 | 0.2147 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.35 s | 208 MiB |
| after | **0.3101** | **0.7592** | 0.0026 | 0.0260 | 0.0940 | 0.5469 | 1.79 s | 813 MiB |

The AFTER arm was re-run after the fix. Its `metrics.json`, `results.json`, `manifest.json` and gold audit are
byte-identical to the pre-fix run; the AFTER timings in the table are from the re-run.

Before Java support, `.java` files yield no symbols, so no context unit reaches the budget: every span and line
recall is 0. With Java, routing reaches 76% of gold, but complete-span recall stays low (2.6% at 4,096 tokens).

Inferred, not measured: the gold spans are large method or region edits in big files, so budget-limited packing
cuts them. The stage counts at 4,096 support this: 22 spans lost at budget, 20 at selection, 33 at entry, 9 at
routing, 3 complete.

This is a 16-task diagnostic with no tuning: the gain is in discovery and routing, not end-to-end span
completeness. Outputs are in [context-before/](context-before/) and [context-after/](context-after/); logs are in
[verification/](verification/).

## Distribution smoke (Linux)

Run before the fix and not repeated. The fix touches no packaging (inferred).

`uv build` produced `oxide-0.0.0-py3-none-any.whl` (SHA-256 `bbe0699a…`) and `oxide-0.0.0.tar.gz`. Each was
installed into its own fresh venv with the locked runtime requirements, then `oxide prepare`, then
`python -I scripts/smoke_dist.py fixtures`. That smoke includes the Java search (`Store.mustGet` first) and the
context check (`static Store open(Mode mode)`).

Both artifacts reported **smoke: OK**: 65 files, 319 entities, search/context, MCP stdio and the store lock
([distribution-wheel.log](verification/distribution-wheel.log),
[distribution-sdist.log](verification/distribution-sdist.log)). Afterwards the repo's `oxide` was still the
editable install.

## Independent re-run (OpenCode GPT-6 Luna)

The same brief, with outputs redirected, was executed end to end by OpenCode (`openai/gpt-6-luna`, `--auto`), which
wrote its own comparison script, oracle and scorer. Outputs are in [../java-v1-opencode/](../java-v1-opencode/).

The first attempt stopped at step 1 on a crash in its own comparison script. It was relaunched with notes on the
file shapes and on what counts as a failed check.

All of its deterministic outputs equal this run's:
- `real/*.json`: `graph_sha256` and resolution counts;
- the audit samples;
- `java-rows.json`;
- both arms' ContextBench `metrics.json` and `results.json`.

Its steps 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 pass with the same numbers; its spot check is 40/40.

Before the fix, its independent javac oracle found the **same single disagreement**: the `@JsonAdapter` class annotation above.
It reported overall precision 14,477 / 14,478 (calls 7,830/7,830, references 5,605/5,606, imports 1,042/1,042).

"""Bounded Java milestone evidence (docs/phase-6/java-v1), without running repository code.

rows PARQUET OUT: the Java tasks of the SHA-checked ContextBench full.parquet selected
  by the rule fixed before scoring (``select``).
fetch ROWS DIR: a ``git archive`` projection of .java and build files per base commit.
context ROWS CORPORA OUT: audit gold, then score with the unchanged ContextBench scorer.
real ROOT OUT: coverage, resolutions, facts parity and persisted edit/rebuild parity.
audit ROOT OUT: SHA-selected resolved cross-file calls and imports, for inspection.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import resource
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tests/python"))
import contextbench as cb
import contextbench_ts as ts
import eval_javascript as ej
import tree_sitter_java
from tree_sitter import Language, Parser

import oxide
from oxide.capture import capture

PER_REPOSITORY = 3
MAX_FILES = 7500
LANGUAGE = Language(tree_sitter_java.language())
DECLARATIONS = (
    "class_declaration",
    "interface_declaration",
    "enum_declaration",
    "record_declaration",
    "annotation_type_declaration",
)
BUILD_FILES = (
    "pom.xml",
    "build.gradle",
    "build.gradle.kts",
    "settings.gradle",
    "settings.gradle.kts",
)


def select(rows: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """The first three Java rows per repository by original instance id whose gold names
    a .java file. Fixed before any scoring; no other filter."""
    chosen: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    taken: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for row in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r["original_inst_id"])):
        gold = json.loads(str(row["gold_context"]))
        if row["language"] != "java" or not any(g["file"].endswith(".java") for g in gold):
            continue
        if taken[str(row["repo"])] < PER_REPOSITORY:
            taken[str(row["repo"])] += 1
            chosen.append(row)
    return chosen


def keep(name: str) -> bool:
    return name.endswith(".java") or Path(name).name in BUILD_FILES


def module_lines(data: bytes) -> set[int]:
    """Lines outside the top-level type declarations (package, imports, comments): the
    scorer's own view through the grammar, independent of OXIDE's derivation."""
    root = Parser(LANGUAGE).parse(data).root_node
    inside = {
        n
        for node in root.named_children
        if node.type in DECLARATIONS
        for n in range(node.start_point[0] + 1, node.end_point[0] + 2)
    }
    return set(range(1, data.count(b"\n") + 2)) - inside


class Lines(cb.Lines):
    def module(self, path: str) -> set[int]:
        if not path.endswith(".java"):
            return super().module(path)
        if path not in self.modules:
            try:
                self.modules[path] = module_lines(self.file(path))
            except OSError:
                self.modules[path] = set()
        return self.modules[path]


def corpus(row: dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return str(row["repo"]).replace("/", "__") + "@" + str(row["base_commit"])[:12]


def context(rows_path: Path, corpora: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    rows = json.loads(rows_path.read_text())
    results, audits, identities, times = [], {}, {}, {}
    for row in rows:
        root = corpora / corpus(row)
        files = sum(1 for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
        assert files <= MAX_FILES, f"{root}: {files} files"
        gold, verdicts = [], []
        for g in json.loads(row["gold_context"]):
            if not g["file"].endswith(".java"):
                continue
            content, numbered = ts.unnumbered(g["content"], g["start_line"])
            start, end = g["start_line"], g["end_line"]
            verdict = cb.classify(root, g["file"], start, end, content, row["patch"])
            verdicts.append(verdict | {"numbered": numbered})
            gold.append(
                {
                    "file": verdict.get("corrected_file", g["file"]),
                    "start": start,
                    "end": end,
                    "sha256": cb._sha(cb.normalized(g["content"])),
                    "class": verdict["class"],
                    "verified": verdict["class"] in cb.VERIFIED,
                }
            )
        task = {
            "id": row["original_inst_id"],
            "split": "heldout",
            "corpus": corpus(row),
            "query": row["problem_statement"],
            "symbols": [],
            "gold": gold,
        }
        audits[task["id"]] = verdicts
        with (
            tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="oxide-contextbench-java-") as temporary,
            oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=Path(temporary)) as repo,
        ):
            report = repo.index()
            started = time.perf_counter()
            result = cb.score(repo, Lines(root), task)
            assert all(
                b["within_budget"] and b["deterministic"] for b in result["bundles"].values()
            )
            results.append(result)
            times[task["id"]] = {
                "index_s": report.seconds,
                "score_s": time.perf_counter() - started,
            }
            identities[task["corpus"]] = {
                "snapshot": report.snapshot.snapshot_id,
                "commit": row["base_commit"],
                "files": report.files,
                "entities": report.entities,
                "relations": report.relations,
                "partial": list(report.partial),
            }
    ej.save(out / "results.json", results)
    ej.save(out / "metrics.json", cb.aggregate(results))
    ej.save(out / "gold-audit.json", audits)
    ej.save(
        out / "manifest.json",
        {
            "source_sha256": cb.PARQUET_SHA256,
            "rows_sha256": hashlib.sha256(rows_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "selection": [r["original_inst_id"] for r in rows],
            "corpora": identities,
            "budgets": cb.BUDGETS,
            "scorer": "contextbench-py-scorer with Java module projection v1",
        },
    )
    ej.save(
        out / "performance.json",
        {"tasks": times, "peak_rss_mib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1024},
    )


def audit(root: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    """Ten resolved cross-file calls and ten resolved imports, chosen by the SHA-256 of
    their evidence, with the caller's text and the target's signature."""
    from oxide.core.indexing import derive

    snap = capture(root)
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in snap.files}
    full = derive(snap, "evaluation")
    entities = {e.key: e for e in full.entities}
    samples = {}
    for kind in ("calls", "imports"):
        edges = [
            (hashlib.sha256(repr(e).encode()).hexdigest(), e, e.evidence)
            for e in full.edges
            if e.kind == kind
            and e.resolution == "resolved"
            and e.evidence is not None
            and e.evidence.path.endswith(".java")
            and not e.targets[0].startswith(f"symbol:{e.evidence.path}#")
        ]
        samples[kind] = [
            {
                "source": e.source,
                "target": e.targets[0],
                "text": data[at.path][at.start : at.end].decode(),
                "target_name": entities[e.targets[0]].name,
                "target_signature": entities[e.targets[0]].signature,
            }
            for _, e, at in sorted(edges, key=lambda t: t[0])[:10]
            if at is not None
        ]
    ej.save(out, samples)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="mode", required=True)
    for mode, names in (
        ("rows", ("parquet", "out")),
        ("fetch", ("rows", "directory")),
        ("context", ("rows", "corpora", "out")),
        ("real", ("root", "out")),
        ("audit", ("root", "out")),
    ):
        mode_parser = sub.add_parser(mode)
        for name in names:
            mode_parser.add_argument(name, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "rows":
        ej.save(args.out, select(cb._parquet(args.parquet)))
    elif args.mode == "fetch":
        ej.fetch(args.rows, args.directory, keep)
    elif args.mode == "context":
        context(args.rows, args.corpora, args.out)
    elif args.mode == "real":
        ej.real(args.root, args.out, "java")
    else:
        audit(args.root, args.out)
## ContextBench diagnostic

Both arms used the same 18 selected rows (`go-rows.json`, SHA-256
`3fdaeb33f815c3da07cd1100762fcb1e1c48dbbc3f1e35f1db3187cd650ecafd`), the same
corpora, gold, and scorer. Before ran the installed previous engine in isolation;
after ran this checkout. Verified gold spans only are scored; the audit classes were
246 exact, 5 contained, 74 path-only, 17 range, 7 drift, and 4 unresolved (the last
three classes are unverified and excluded from verified metrics).

| Verified macro metric (18 tasks, 325 spans, 9,077 lines) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Entry recall@20 | 0.187655 | 0.128309 |
| Routed coverage | 0.187655 | 0.357206 |
| Complete span recall@1,024 | 0 | 0.020373 |
| Complete span recall@4,096 | 0 | 0.047976 |
| Line recall@4,096 | 0 | 0.076386 |

The lower entry recall@20 is retained as observed; no parameters were tuned. Median
index time across the 18 tasks was 0.132 s before and 1.471 s after; peak process RSS
was 162.6 MiB and 385.8 MiB. This is a small diagnostic (n=18), not a gate, broad
quality claim, or reason to tune retrieval. Raw scores, audits, corpus identities,
timings and integrity records are in `context-before/` and `context-after/`.

## Successor baselines, limitations and verification

`baseline-v10` and `typescript-v7` are identity-only successors for the derivation
identity change. Results otherwise match their predecessors, metrics are byte-identical,
and each manifest corpus record changed only in its derivation hash. The Go limitations
are documented in [../../go.md](../../go.md). The `go/types` oracle covers gin only (above). Windows
and macOS Go runtime and artifact checks remain pending hosted CI; wheel availability
does not establish runtime support. The platform matrix and existing LadybugDB limits
still apply.

Reproduce from a locked checkout, under the resource caps recorded in the evaluation
logs:

```sh
mise run verify
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_go.py real /path/to/gin docs/phase-6/go-v1/real/gin.json
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_go.py audit /path/to/gin docs/phase-6/go-v1/real/gin-audit.json
uv run --locked python scripts/bench.py /path/to/gin --iterations 3 --warm 3 --query ServeHTTP --query Bind
uv run --locked python scripts/eval_go.py context /path/to/go-rows.json /path/to/corpora docs/phase-6/go-v1/context-after
# go/types oracle: needs a Go 1.27 toolchain; writes gin-uses.json, then gin-oracle.json and report.md
cp docs/phase-6/go-v1/oracle/* /path/to/work/ && (cd /path/to/work && go run . /path/to/gin gin-uses.json)
uv run --locked python docs/phase-6/go-v1/oracle/score.py /path/to/work /path/to/gin
```

The previous-engine ContextBench arm requires its recorded isolated environment and
the same rows and corpora. Distribution smoke follows
[platforms.md](../../platforms.md). Next language priority: Rust, then reassess Java
or C# against a scoped fixture and resolution oracle.

        files = sum(1 for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
        assert files <= MAX_FILES, f"{root}: {files} files"

            content, numbered = ts.unnumbered(g["content"], g["start_line"])

            gold.append(

                    "end": end,

                    "class": verdict["class"],

            "split": "heldout",

            "query": row["problem_statement"],

                "relations": report.relations,
                "partial": list(report.partial),

            "corpora": identities,

"""Bounded C++ ContextBench diagnostic (docs/phase-6/cpp-v1), without running repository code.

rows PARQUET OUT: the C++ tasks of the SHA-checked ContextBench full.parquet selected
  by the rule fixed before scoring (``select``).
fetch ROWS DIR: a ``git archive`` projection of C/C++ sources and build files per base commit.
context ROWS CORPORA OUT: audit gold, then score with the unchanged ContextBench scorer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import resource
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tests/python"))
import contextbench as cb
import contextbench_ts as ts
import eval_javascript as ej
import tree_sitter_cpp
from tree_sitter import Language, Node, Parser

import oxide

PER_REPOSITORY = 3
MAX_FILES = 7500
LANGUAGE = Language(tree_sitter_cpp.language())
# docs/cpp.md's C++ extensions, plus .h (C or C++ by content) and .c.
SOURCES = (
    ".cc", ".cpp", ".cxx", ".c++", ".hh", ".hpp", ".hxx", ".h++", ".ipp", ".tpp", ".inl",
    ".h", ".c",
)  # fmt: skip
BUILD_FILES = ("CMakeLists.txt", "meson.build", "Makefile", "BUILD", "BUILD.bazel")
DECLARATIONS = (
    "function_definition",
    "template_declaration",
    "class_specifier",
    "struct_specifier",
    "union_specifier",
    "enum_specifier",
)
CONTAINERS = ("namespace_definition", "linkage_specification")


def select(rows: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """The first three C++ rows per repository by original instance id whose gold names
    a C/C++ source file. Fixed before any scoring; no other filter."""
    chosen: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    taken: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for row in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r["original_inst_id"])):
        gold = json.loads(str(row["gold_context"]))
        if row["language"] != "cpp" or not any(g["file"].endswith(SOURCES) for g in gold):
            continue
        if taken[str(row["repo"])] < PER_REPOSITORY:
            taken[str(row["repo"])] += 1
            chosen.append(row)
    return chosen


def keep(name: str) -> bool:
    return name.endswith(SOURCES) or Path(name).name in BUILD_FILES


def module_lines(data: bytes) -> set[int]:
    """Lines outside the outermost function, template and class/struct/union/enum
    definitions (those inside namespaces and ``extern "C"`` blocks included): the scorer's
    own view through the grammar, independent of OXIDE's derivation. Macros stay opaque."""
    root = Parser(LANGUAGE).parse(data).root_node
    inside: set[int] = set()
    pending: list[Node] = list(root.named_children)
    while pending:
        node = pending.pop()
        if node.type in DECLARATIONS:
            inside.update(range(node.start_point[0] + 1, node.end_point[0] + 2))
        elif node.type in CONTAINERS:
            body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
            pending.extend(body.named_children if body is not None else [])
    return set(range(1, data.count(b"\n") + 2)) - inside


class Lines(cb.Lines):
    def module(self, path: str) -> set[int]:
        if not path.endswith(SOURCES):
            return super().module(path)
        if path not in self.modules:
            try:
                self.modules[path] = module_lines(self.file(path))
            except OSError:
                self.modules[path] = set()
        return self.modules[path]


def corpus(row: dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return str(row["repo"]).replace("/", "__") + "@" + str(row["base_commit"])[:12]


def context(rows_path: Path, corpora: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    rows = json.loads(rows_path.read_text())
    results, audits, identities, times = [], {}, {}, {}
    for row in rows:
        root = corpora / corpus(row)
        files = sum(1 for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
        assert files <= MAX_FILES, f"{root}: {files} files"
        gold, verdicts = [], []
        for g in json.loads(row["gold_context"]):
            if not g["file"].endswith(SOURCES):
                continue
            content, numbered = ts.unnumbered(g["content"], g["start_line"])
            start, end = g["start_line"], g["end_line"]
            verdict = cb.classify(root, g["file"], start, end, content, row["patch"])
            verdicts.append(verdict | {"numbered": numbered})
            gold.append(
                {
                    "file": verdict.get("corrected_file", g["file"]),
                    "start": start,
                    "end": end,
                    "sha256": cb._sha(cb.normalized(g["content"])),
                    "class": verdict["class"],
                    "verified": verdict["class"] in cb.VERIFIED,
                }
            )
        task = {
            "id": row["original_inst_id"],
            "split": "heldout",
            "corpus": corpus(row),
            "query": row["problem_statement"],
            "symbols": [],
            "gold": gold,
        }
        audits[task["id"]] = verdicts
        with (
            tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="oxide-contextbench-cpp-") as temporary,
            oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=Path(temporary)) as repo,
        ):
            report = repo.index()
            started = time.perf_counter()
            result = cb.score(repo, Lines(root), task)
            assert all(
                b["within_budget"] and b["deterministic"] for b in result["bundles"].values()
            )
            results.append(result)
            times[task["id"]] = {
                "index_s": report.seconds,
                "score_s": time.perf_counter() - started,
            }
            identities[task["corpus"]] = {
                "snapshot": report.snapshot.snapshot_id,
                "commit": row["base_commit"],
                "files": report.files,
                "entities": report.entities,
                "relations": report.relations,
                "partial": list(report.partial),
            }
    ej.save(out / "results.json", results)
    ej.save(out / "metrics.json", cb.aggregate(results))
    ej.save(out / "gold-audit.json", audits)
    ej.save(
        out / "manifest.json",
        {
            "source_sha256": cb.PARQUET_SHA256,
            "rows_sha256": hashlib.sha256(rows_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "selection": [r["original_inst_id"] for r in rows],
            "corpora": identities,
            "budgets": cb.BUDGETS,
            "scorer": "contextbench-py-scorer with C++ module projection v1",
        },
    )
    ej.save(
        out / "performance.json",
        {"tasks": times, "peak_rss_mib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1024},
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="mode", required=True)
    for mode, names in (
        ("rows", ("parquet", "out")),
        ("fetch", ("rows", "directory")),
        ("context", ("rows", "corpora", "out")),
    ):
        mode_parser = sub.add_parser(mode)
        for name in names:
            mode_parser.add_argument(name, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "rows":
        ej.save(args.out, select(cb._parquet(args.parquet)))
    elif args.mode == "fetch":
        ej.fetch(args.rows, args.directory, keep)
    else:
        context(args.rows, args.corpora, args.out)

"""Bounded C++ ContextBench diagnostic (docs/phase-6/cpp-v1), without running repository code.

rows PARQUET OUT: the C++ tasks of the SHA-checked ContextBench full.parquet selected
  by the rule fixed before scoring (``select``).
fetch ROWS DIR: a ``git archive`` projection of C/C++ sources and build files per base commit.
context ROWS CORPORA OUT: audit gold, then score with the unchanged ContextBench scorer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import resource
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tests/python"))
import contextbench as cb
import contextbench_ts as ts
import eval_javascript as ej
import tree_sitter_cpp
from tree_sitter import Language, Node, Parser

import oxide

PER_REPOSITORY = 3
MAX_FILES = 7500
LANGUAGE = Language(tree_sitter_cpp.language())
# docs/cpp.md's C++ extensions, plus .h (C or C++ by content) and .c.
SOURCES = (
    ".cc", ".cpp", ".cxx", ".c++", ".hh", ".hpp", ".hxx", ".h++", ".ipp", ".tpp", ".inl",
    ".h", ".c",
)  # fmt: skip
BUILD_FILES = ("CMakeLists.txt", "meson.build", "Makefile", "BUILD", "BUILD.bazel")
DECLARATIONS = (
    "function_definition",
    "template_declaration",
    "class_specifier",
    "struct_specifier",
    "union_specifier",
    "enum_specifier",
)
CONTAINERS = ("namespace_definition", "linkage_specification")


def select(rows: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """The first three C++ rows per repository by original instance id whose gold names
    a C/C++ source file. Fixed before any scoring; no other filter."""
    chosen: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    taken: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for row in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r["original_inst_id"])):
        gold = json.loads(str(row["gold_context"]))
        if row["language"] != "cpp" or not any(g["file"].endswith(SOURCES) for g in gold):
            continue
        if taken[str(row["repo"])] < PER_REPOSITORY:
            taken[str(row["repo"])] += 1
            chosen.append(row)
    return chosen


def keep(name: str) -> bool:
    return name.endswith(SOURCES) or Path(name).name in BUILD_FILES


def module_lines(data: bytes) -> set[int]:
    """Lines outside the outermost function, template and class/struct/union/enum
    definitions (those inside namespaces and ``extern "C"`` blocks included): the scorer's
    own view through the grammar, independent of OXIDE's derivation. Macros stay opaque."""
    root = Parser(LANGUAGE).parse(data).root_node
    inside: set[int] = set()
    pending: list[Node] = list(root.named_children)
    while pending:
        node = pending.pop()
        if node.type in DECLARATIONS:
            inside.update(range(node.start_point[0] + 1, node.end_point[0] + 2))
        elif node.type in CONTAINERS:
            body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
            pending.extend(body.named_children if body is not None else [])
    return set(range(1, data.count(b"\n") + 2)) - inside


class Lines(cb.Lines):
    def module(self, path: str) -> set[int]:
        if not path.endswith(SOURCES):
            return super().module(path)
        if path not in self.modules:
            try:
                self.modules[path] = module_lines(self.file(path))
            except OSError:
                self.modules[path] = set()
        return self.modules[path]


def corpus(row: dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return str(row["repo"]).replace("/", "__") + "@" + str(row["base_commit"])[:12]


def context(rows_path: Path, corpora: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    rows = json.loads(rows_path.read_text())
    results, audits, identities, times = [], {}, {}, {}
    for row in rows:
        root = corpora / corpus(row)
        files = sum(1 for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
        assert files <= MAX_FILES, f"{root}: {files} files"
        gold, verdicts = [], []
        for g in json.loads(row["gold_context"]):
            if not g["file"].endswith(SOURCES):
                continue
            content, numbered = ts.unnumbered(g["content"], g["start_line"])
            start, end = g["start_line"], g["end_line"]
            verdict = cb.classify(root, g["file"], start, end, content, row["patch"])
            verdicts.append(verdict | {"numbered": numbered})
            gold.append(
                {
                    "file": verdict.get("corrected_file", g["file"]),
                    "start": start,
                    "end": end,
                    "sha256": cb._sha(cb.normalized(g["content"])),
                    "class": verdict["class"],
                    "verified": verdict["class"] in cb.VERIFIED,
                }
            )
        task = {
            "id": row["original_inst_id"],
            "split": "heldout",
            "corpus": corpus(row),
            "query": row["problem_statement"],
            "symbols": [],
            "gold": gold,
        }
        audits[task["id"]] = verdicts
        with (
            tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="oxide-contextbench-cpp-") as temporary,
            oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=Path(temporary)) as repo,
        ):
            report = repo.index()
            started = time.perf_counter()
            result = cb.score(repo, Lines(root), task)
            assert all(
                b["within_budget"] and b["deterministic"] for b in result["bundles"].values()
            )
            results.append(result)
            times[task["id"]] = {
                "index_s": report.seconds,
                "score_s": time.perf_counter() - started,
            }
            identities[task["corpus"]] = {
                "snapshot": report.snapshot.snapshot_id,
                "commit": row["base_commit"],
                "files": report.files,
                "entities": report.entities,
                "relations": report.relations,
                "partial": list(report.partial),
            }
    ej.save(out / "results.json", results)
    ej.save(out / "metrics.json", cb.aggregate(results))
    ej.save(out / "gold-audit.json", audits)
    ej.save(
        out / "manifest.json",
        {
            "source_sha256": cb.PARQUET_SHA256,
            "rows_sha256": hashlib.sha256(rows_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "selection": [r["original_inst_id"] for r in rows],
            "corpora": identities,
            "budgets": cb.BUDGETS,
            "scorer": "contextbench-py-scorer with C++ module projection v1",
        },
    )
    ej.save(
        out / "performance.json",
        {"tasks": times, "peak_rss_mib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1024},
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="mode", required=True)
    for mode, names in (
        ("rows", ("parquet", "out")),
        ("fetch", ("rows", "directory")),
        ("context", ("rows", "corpora", "out")),
    ):
        mode_parser = sub.add_parser(mode)
        for name in names:
            mode_parser.add_argument(name, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "rows":
        ej.save(args.out, select(cb._parquet(args.parquet)))
    elif args.mode == "fetch":
        ej.fetch(args.rows, args.directory, keep)
    else:
        context(args.rows, args.corpora, args.out)

content.content:
# cpp-v1: C++ language slice evidence

The C++ slice (`oxide-cpp-v1`, [../../cpp.md](../../cpp.md)) is judged against G++, which
binds every direct call the way the build does. `oracle/oracle.py` compiles each
translation unit with `g++ -O0 -fcallgraph-info` and reads every direct call: its file
and line, the callee's mangled name and the definition GCC kept (a callee's definition is
where a unit that defines it, per `nm`, places it). G++'s call column is not the call's
own (calls in another call's arguments carry that call's `(`, a temporary its `)`), so
each oxide `calls` edge is matched to the GCC callees of the same unqualified name
(`c++filt -p`) on the line of its `(`. A resolved edge agrees when its target is a
function or method whose source holds such a callee's definition line, for every such
callee a compiled unit defines (a template's call site binds once per instantiation;
"agree for some" is reported apart). A resolved prototype whose callee no compiled unit
defines there is checked against the declaration GCC kept. Edges to macros, which GCC
sees expanded, are counted and not judged. Measured with g++ 16.2.1.

Corpora (sources outside the repository, `~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/cpp-v1`), each
captured whole (tests, bundled gtest/gmock and docs included):
- yaml-cpp 0.8.0 (`yaml-cpp.tgz`, sha256 `fbe74bbd…3a16`): the 31 units of `src/` and
  `src/contrib/`, `-std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc`;
- fmt 11.1.4 (`fmt.tgz`, sha256 `ac366b7b…1e1e`): `src/format.cc`, `src/os.cc`, every
  `test/*-test.cc`, the test utilities and the bundled `gmock-gtest-all.cc`,

| Complete span recall@1,024 | 0.006993 | 0 |

| Line recall@4,096 | 0.034005 | 0.040730 |

before and has no entry now) and simdjson-1695. Neither direction is significant at
n=11; it is retained as observed, nothing was tuned. Median index time was 1.23 s
before and 3.88 s after; peak RSS 228 and 280 MiB. This is a small diagnostic, not a
gate. Raw scores, audits, corpus identities and timings are in `context-before/` and
`context-after/`.

# cpp-v1: C++ language slice evidence

The C++ slice (`oxide-cpp-v1`, [../../cpp.md](../../cpp.md)) is judged against G++, which
binds every direct call the way the build does. `oracle/oracle.py` compiles each
translation unit with `g++ -O0 -fcallgraph-info` and reads every direct call: its file
and line, the callee's mangled name and the definition GCC kept (a callee's definition is
where a unit that defines it, per `nm`, places it). G++'s call column is not the call's
own (calls in another call's arguments carry that call's `(`, a temporary its `)`), so
each oxide `calls` edge is matched to the GCC callees of the same unqualified name
(`c++filt -p`) on the line of its `(`. A resolved edge agrees when its target is a
function or method whose source holds such a callee's definition line, for every such
callee a compiled unit defines (a template's call site binds once per instantiation;
"agree for some" is reported apart). A resolved prototype whose callee no compiled unit
defines there is checked against the declaration GCC kept. Edges to macros, which GCC
sees expanded, are counted and not judged. Measured with g++ 16.2.1.

Corpora (sources outside the repository, `~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/cpp-v1`), each
captured whole (tests, bundled gtest/gmock and docs included):
- yaml-cpp 0.8.0 (`yaml-cpp.tgz`, sha256 `fbe74bbd…3a16`): the 31 units of `src/` and
  `src/contrib/`, `-std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc`;
- fmt 11.1.4 (`fmt.tgz`, sha256 `ac366b7b…1e1e`): `src/format.cc`, `src/os.cc`, every
  `test/*-test.cc`, the test utilities and the bundled `gmock-gtest-all.cc`,
  `-std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint`
  (28 units; `format-impl-test.cc`, `header-only-test.cc` and `module-test.cc` do not
  compile with these flags and are skipped).

## Results (measured)

| Tally | yaml-cpp | fmt |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| G++ calls to a captured definition (in units / in headers) | 1,491 / 726 | 36,748 / 45,708 |
| resolved, agree | **640** | **2,244** |
| resolved, disagree | **0** | **7** |
| resolved, agree for some instantiations or overloads on the line | 8 | 1 |
| resolved, callee defined in no compiled unit | 0 | 15 |
| resolved to a macro / ambiguous to a macro, not judged | 7,950 / 81 | 2,883 / 420 |
| ambiguous, GCC binds a captured definition | 66 | 611 |
| unresolved, GCC binds a captured definition | 0 | 2,083 |
| unresolved, GCC binds an external one / one no unit compiles | 15 / 1 | 281 / 346 |
| no GCC call of that name on the line (resolved, ambiguous, unresolved) | 7,941 / 1,229 / 17,650 | 1,168 / 338 / 3,551 |

Precision on judged resolved edges is 1.0 on yaml-cpp and 0.997 on fmt. The 7 fmt
disagreements, characterized:
- 3 are `FMT_POSIX_CALL(dup(fd))`-style calls inside a class with a `dup` member: the
  macro makes them `::dup` (or the test build's `test::dup`); macro expansion is not
  modeled;
- 1 is argument-dependent lookup (`format_as(value)` binds a function in the argument
  type's namespace), not modeled;
- 1 is in the gtest amalgamation, where parse errors lost a namespace's nesting, so the
  call bound the header's prototype of the same function under another qualified name;
- 2 are templates: `formatter<string_view>::format(...)` drops its template argument, so
  it binds the enclosing `formatter<throws_on_move>` specialization's own `format`; and a
  `scan_data<…>()` constructor bound to another constructor of the same arity.

The "agree for some" cases are lines that call two overloads of one name (`RegEx(' ') |
RegEx("\r\n")`, gtest's `Message` copy and default constructors) or a template
instantiated so that its call binds differently; the oracle cannot separate them by line.
Recall is low by design: most G++ calls to captured definitions go through objects
(`x.f()`, `p->f()`) and need types, which the slice does not record (docs/cpp.md); "no
GCC call" edges sit in code no compiled unit instantiates or includes (templates, test
helpers, bundled gtest), or in macro arguments G++ reports elsewhere.

Every disagreement found while building the slice was traced and fixed or explained
before these numbers. Fixed in the slice: C's "every external definition" linkage rule
bound fmt's own `fprintf` template to libc calls in units that never declare it (C++
calls now need a visible declaration); default arguments on a prototype made its
out-of-line definition look too strict (arity is shared by declarations of the same
parameter count); and the unexpanded-macro idioms in docs/cpp.md, which had folded most
of `fmt/format.h` into one parse error. Fixed in the oracle: G++'s columns, unit-prefixed
internal symbols, and callees defined in units first left uncompiled.

The C slice's GCC oracle is unchanged by this slice: Lua 3,036 agree / 0 disagree,
hiredis in Redis 975 / 0 ([../c-v1](../c-v1/README.md)). Of Redis's 274 `.h` files, the two
Qt adapter headers (`deps/hiredis/adapters/qt.h`, `examples/example-qt.h`) are now C++;
Lua's 27 stay C.

Coverage and cost (measured, `derive` only, 200% CPU cap): fmt 69 C++ files, 44
complete and 25 partial, 1.3 s; yaml-cpp 246 C++ files (bundled gtest included), 183
complete and 63 partial, 2.1 s.

Not measured: retrieval or context quality on C++ tasks. ContextBench holds 60 C++
rows (fmt, nlohmann/json, simdjson, Catch2, ponyc, …), but no diagnostic was run; the
pinned baseline corpora hold no C++, and their baselines move by identity only
([../baseline-v17](../baseline-v17/README.md), [../typescript-v14](../typescript-v14/README.md)).

## Verification (Linux, measured)

Logs are in [verification/](verification/):
- `mise-verify.log`: ruff clean, mypy `--strict` clean (78 files), pytest 425 passed,
  7 skipped, `test_baseline.py` against baseline-v17 included.
- `distribution-wheel.log`, `distribution-sdist.log`: both artifacts install, index the
  fixtures (82 files, 403 entities) and pass `scripts/smoke_dist.py` (`exit=0`). The first
  run failed: the copied C++ fixture's two `Store::must_get` entities ranked above Rust's
  `<impl Store>.must_get`, which the Rust check required at rank 1; it now requires the
  Rust entity among the results (extraction unchanged).
- `contextbench-ts.log`: `mise run contextbench-ts` against typescript-v14, 17 passed
  (14 min, 200% CPU / 3 GB cap).

## Reproduce

```
uv run python docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/oracle.py $YAML docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/yaml-cpp-oracle.json 'src/*.cpp' 'src/contrib/*.cpp' -- -std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc
uv run python docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/oracle.py $FMT docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/fmt-oracle.json 'src/format.cc' 'src/os.cc' 'test/*-test.cc' 'test/gtest-extra.cc' 'test/util.cc' 'test/test-main.cc' 'test/gtest/gmock-gtest-all.cc' -- -std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint
```

`*-oracle.json` lists every disagreement (with "agree for some"), every miss (`missed`)
and every resolved edge in a unit without a GCC call of its name (`unseen`);
`*-oracle.log` is the printed tally.
