# cpp-v1: C++ language slice evidence

The C++ slice (`oxide-cpp-v1`, [../../cpp.md](../../cpp.md)) is judged against G++, which
binds every direct call the way the build does. `oracle/oracle.py` compiles each
translation unit with `g++ -O0 -fcallgraph-info` and reads every direct call: its file
and line, the callee's mangled name and the definition GCC kept (a callee's definition is
where a unit that defines it, per `nm`, places it). G++'s call column is not the call's
own (calls in another call's arguments carry that call's `(`, a temporary its `)`), so
each oxide `calls` edge is matched to the GCC callees of the same unqualified name
(`c++filt -p`) on the line of its `(`. A resolved edge agrees when its target is a
function or method whose source holds such a callee's definition line, for every such
callee a compiled unit defines (a template's call site binds once per instantiation;
"agree for some" is reported apart). A resolved prototype whose callee no compiled unit
defines there is checked against the declaration GCC kept. Edges to macros, which GCC
sees expanded, are counted and not judged. Measured with g++ 16.2.1.

Corpora (sources outside the repository, `~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/cpp-v1`), each
captured whole (tests, bundled gtest/gmock and docs included):
- yaml-cpp 0.8.0 (`yaml-cpp.tgz`, sha256 `fbe74bbd…3a16`): the 31 units of `src/` and
  `src/contrib/`, `-std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc`;
- fmt 11.1.4 (`fmt.tgz`, sha256 `ac366b7b…1e1e`): `src/format.cc`, `src/os.cc`, every
  `test/*-test.cc`, the test utilities and the bundled `gmock-gtest-all.cc`,
  `-std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint`
  (28 units; `format-impl-test.cc`, `header-only-test.cc` and `module-test.cc` do not
  compile with these flags and are skipped).

## Results (measured)

| Tally | yaml-cpp | fmt |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| G++ calls to a captured definition (in units / in headers) | 1,491 / 726 | 36,748 / 45,708 |
| resolved, agree | **640** | **2,244** |
| resolved, disagree | **0** | **7** |
| resolved, agree for some instantiations or overloads on the line | 8 | 1 |
| resolved, callee defined in no compiled unit | 0 | 15 |
| resolved to a macro / ambiguous to a macro, not judged | 7,950 / 81 | 2,883 / 420 |
| ambiguous, GCC binds a captured definition | 66 | 611 |
| unresolved, GCC binds a captured definition | 0 | 2,083 |
| unresolved, GCC binds an external one / one no unit compiles | 15 / 1 | 281 / 346 |
| no GCC call of that name on the line (resolved, ambiguous, unresolved) | 7,941 / 1,229 / 17,650 | 1,168 / 338 / 3,551 |

Precision on judged resolved edges is 1.0 on yaml-cpp and 0.997 on fmt. The 7 fmt
disagreements, characterized:
- 3 are `FMT_POSIX_CALL(dup(fd))`-style calls inside a class with a `dup` member: the
  macro makes them `::dup` (or the test build's `test::dup`); macro expansion is not
  modeled;
- 1 is argument-dependent lookup (`format_as(value)` binds a function in the argument
  type's namespace), not modeled;
- 1 is in the gtest amalgamation, where parse errors lost a namespace's nesting, so the
  call bound the header's prototype of the same function under another qualified name;
- 2 are templates: `formatter<string_view>::format(...)` drops its template argument, so
  it binds the enclosing `formatter<throws_on_move>` specialization's own `format`; and a
  `scan_data<…>()` constructor bound to another constructor of the same arity.

The "agree for some" cases are lines that call two overloads of one name (`RegEx(' ') |
RegEx("\r\n")`, gtest's `Message` copy and default constructors) or a template
instantiated so that its call binds differently; the oracle cannot separate them by line.
Recall is low by design: most G++ calls to captured definitions go through objects
(`x.f()`, `p->f()`) and need types, which the slice does not record (docs/cpp.md); "no
GCC call" edges sit in code no compiled unit instantiates or includes (templates, test
helpers, bundled gtest), or in macro arguments G++ reports elsewhere.

Every disagreement found while building the slice was traced and fixed or explained
before these numbers. Fixed in the slice: C's "every external definition" linkage rule
bound fmt's own `fprintf` template to libc calls in units that never declare it (C++
calls now need a visible declaration); default arguments on a prototype made its
out-of-line definition look too strict (arity is shared by declarations of the same
parameter count); and the unexpanded-macro idioms in docs/cpp.md, which had folded most
of `fmt/format.h` into one parse error. Fixed in the oracle: G++'s columns, unit-prefixed
internal symbols, and callees defined in units first left uncompiled.

The C slice's GCC oracle is unchanged by this slice: Lua 3,036 agree / 0 disagree,
hiredis in Redis 975 / 0 ([../c-v1](../c-v1/README.md)). Of Redis's 274 `.h` files, the two
Qt adapter headers (`deps/hiredis/adapters/qt.h`, `examples/example-qt.h`) are now C++;
Lua's 27 stay C.

Coverage and cost (measured, `derive` only, 200% CPU cap): fmt 69 C++ files, 44
complete and 25 partial, 1.3 s; yaml-cpp 246 C++ files (bundled gtest included), 183
complete and 63 partial, 2.1 s.

The pinned baseline corpora hold no C++, and their baselines move by identity only
([../baseline-v17](../baseline-v17/README.md), [../typescript-v14](../typescript-v14/README.md)).

## ContextBench diagnostic (measured)

`scripts/eval_cpp.py` selected, before any scoring, the first three C++ rows per
repository (by instance id) whose gold names a C/C++ source: 12 rows over Catch2, fmt,
nlohmann/json and simdjson (`cpp-rows.json`, SHA-256
`1627c229fc27e7315927a5716550c84982362a86e6e19918d7b17a368f6f4e9b`). Corpora are a
`git archive` projection of C/C++ sources and build files at each base commit (65–376
files). Both arms used the same rows, corpora, gold audit and scorer, with module lines
projected through tree-sitter-cpp independently of OXIDE. Before ran the previous engine
(18ffaa5, C slice only, `.h` parsed as C) with this checkout's scorer and environment;
after ran this checkout. Gold audit: 16 exact, 59 path-only, 4 unresolved (excluded);
Catch2-1422 has no verified span.

| Verified macro metric (11 tasks, 75 spans, 6,021 lines) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Entry recall@20 | 0.267796 | 0.241872 |
| Routed coverage | 0.552564 | 0.484739 |
| Complete span recall@1,024 | 0.006993 | 0 |
| Complete span recall@4,096 | 0.006993 | 0.039960 |
| Line recall@4,096 | 0.034005 | 0.040730 |
| File recall@4,096 | 0.337413 | 0.406177 |

The C++ slice indexes 2–10× more entities (Catch2 587 → 6,560, nlohmann/json 678 →
6,511). Entry recall@20 rises on all three fmt tasks (0.43/0.09/0.12 → 0.57/0.45/0.50)
and Catch2-1448 (0.50 → 0.75), and falls on nlohmann/json-1221 (its one span, the whole
`exceptions.hpp`, ranked 15th before and has no entry now), json-1301 and
simdjson-1695. Neither direction is meaningful at n=11; the results are retained as
observed and nothing was tuned. Median index time was 1.23 s before and 3.88 s after;
peak RSS 228 and 280 MiB (200% CPU / 3 GB cap). This is a small diagnostic, not a gate.
Raw scores, audits, corpus identities and timings are in `context-before/` and
`context-after/`.

## Verification (Linux, measured)

Logs are in [verification/](verification/):
- `mise-verify.log`: ruff clean, mypy `--strict` clean (78 files), pytest 425 passed,
  7 skipped, `test_baseline.py` against baseline-v17 included.
- `distribution-wheel.log`, `distribution-sdist.log`: both artifacts install, index the
  fixtures (82 files, 403 entities) and pass `scripts/smoke_dist.py` (`exit=0`). The first
  run failed: the copied C++ fixture's two `Store::must_get` entities ranked above Rust's
  `<impl Store>.must_get`, which the Rust check required at rank 1; it now requires the
  Rust entity among the results (extraction unchanged).
- `contextbench-ts.log`: `mise run contextbench-ts` against typescript-v14, 17 passed
  (14 min, 200% CPU / 3 GB cap).

## Reproduce

```
uv run python docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/oracle.py $YAML docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/yaml-cpp-oracle.json 'src/*.cpp' 'src/contrib/*.cpp' -- -std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc
uv run python docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/oracle.py $FMT docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/oracle/fmt-oracle.json 'src/format.cc' 'src/os.cc' 'test/*-test.cc' 'test/gtest-extra.cc' 'test/util.cc' 'test/test-main.cc' 'test/gtest/gmock-gtest-all.cc' -- -std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint
```

`*-oracle.json` lists every disagreement (with "agree for some"), every miss (`missed`)
and every resolved edge in a unit without a GCC call of its name (`unseen`);
`*-oracle.log` is the printed tally.

aiTitle: OXIDE repo cleanup and rewrite/v2 merge readiness

content.text:
The cleaned tree passes `mise run verify` (Ruff clean, mypy `--strict` clean on 78 files, 425 passed, 7 skipped), and the C++ retrieval check is done. Its result is mixed: about as many tasks got better as worse. Nothing is committed yet, and three decisions are yours before `rewrite/v2` can go into `main`.

**C++ retrieval and context quality.** I added `scripts/eval_cpp.py` (197 lines), which works the same way as the Go, Java and Rust evals. It picked 12 C++ tasks from ContextBench before any scoring: 3 each from Catch2, fmt, nlohmann/json and simdjson. Each task was scored twice with the same scorer: once on the engine before C++ support (commit 18ffaa5, which reads `.h` files as C) and once on this checkout. 11 tasks had usable gold answers.

| Metric (11 tasks, 75 gold spans) | Before C++ | Now |
|---|---:|---:|
| Entry recall@20 | 0.268 | 0.242 |
| Routed coverage | 0.553 | 0.485 |
| Complete span recall@4,096 | 0.007 | 0.040 |
| Line recall@4,096 | 0.034 | 0.041 |
| File recall@4,096 | 0.337 | 0.406 |

- **Better:** all three fmt tasks and Catch2-1448.
- **Worse:** nlohmann/json-1221, whose only gold answer is the whole `exceptions.hpp` file; it ranked 15th before and is not found at all now. json-1301 and simdjson-1695 also got worse.
- **Cost:** C++ support indexes 2–10× more symbols. Median index time went from 1.23 s to 3.88 s, and peak memory from 228 to 280 MiB.

With 11 tasks, neither direction means much. I recorded the numbers as they came out and changed no retrieval settings. The write-up, table and rerun commands are in `docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/README.md`, with the raw results in `context-before/` and `context-after/`. The "C++ quality not measured" note there is gone.

**Cleanup.** I removed the temporary worktree used for the "before" run and its scratch folder. The earlier cleanup (junk files deleted, stale `typescript-v8` references fixed) still stands. The TypeScript check passed on its own run (17 passed).

**Merging.** `main` is an ancestor of `rewrite/v2`, so the merge is a plain fast-forward once the work is committed. CI is green on HEAD `64ee0de`.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **`pyrefly` dev dependency** in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`: verify doesn't use it. Keep it and document it, or drop it?
2. **Evidence files to commit:** the C++ results above plus `scripts/eval_cpp.py`, `docs/phase-6/cpp-v1/verification/contextbench-ts.log`, `docs/phase-6/go-v1/oracle/` and `docs/phase-6/rust-v1/rust-rows.json`. The Go and Rust READMEs link to the last two, so they should be in the repo.
3. **Your local tool files:** `.mcp.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.entire/agent-guide.md`, `.agents/skills/oxide-eval-freeze/` and `docs/oxide-architecture.html`. Which belong in the repo?

Not checked: the eval script uses the test harness's private helpers and isn't covered by verify, which lints only `src/` and `tests/`; I ran Ruff on it by hand. The "before" run used the old engine with this checkout's Python environment, because the old environment can't load the C++ parser the scorer needs.

# cpp-v1: C++ language slice evidence

The C++ slice (`oxide-cpp-v1`, [../../cpp.md](../../cpp.md)) is judged against G++, which
binds every direct call the way the build does. `oracle/oracle.py` compiles each
translation unit with `g++ -O0 -fcallgraph-info` and reads every direct call: its file
and line, the callee's mangled name and the definition GCC kept (a callee's definition is
where a unit that defines it, per `nm`, places it). G++'s call column is not the call's
own (calls in another call's arguments carry that call's `(`, a temporary its `)`), so
each oxide `calls` edge is matched to the GCC callees of the same unqualified name
(`c++filt -p`) on the line of its `(`. A resolved edge agrees when its target is a
function or method whose source holds such a callee's definition line, for every such
callee a compiled unit defines (a template's call site binds once per instantiation;
"agree for some" is reported apart). A resolved prototype whose callee no compiled unit
defines there is checked against the declaration GCC kept. Edges to macros, which GCC
sees expanded, are counted and not judged. Measured with g++ 16.2.1.

Corpora (sources outside the repository, `~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/cpp-v1`), each
captured whole (tests, bundled gtest/gmock and docs included):
- yaml-cpp 0.8.0 (`yaml-cpp.tgz`, sha256 `fbe74bbd…3a16`): the 31 units of `src/` and
  `src/contrib/`, `-std=c++17 -include cstdint -Iinclude -Isrc`;
- fmt 11.1.4 (`fmt.tgz`, sha256 `ac366b7b…1e1e`): `src/format.cc`, `src/os.cc`, every
  `test/*-test.cc`, the test utilities and the bundled `gmock-gtest-all.cc`,
  `-std=c++17 -Iinclude -Itest -Itest/gtest -DGTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING=1 -include cstdint`
  (28 units; `format-impl-test.cc`, `header-only-test.cc` and `module-test.cc` do not
  compile with these flags and are skipped).

## Results (measured)

| Tally | yaml-cpp | fmt |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| G++ calls to a captured definition (in units / in headers) | 1,491 / 726 | 36,748 / 45,708 |
| resolved, agree | **640** | **2,244** |
| resolved, disagree | **0** | **7** |
| resolved, agree for some instantiations or overloads on the line | 8 | 1 |
| resolved, callee defined in no compiled unit | 0 | 15 |
| resolved to a macro / ambiguous to a macro, not judged | 7,950 / 81 | 2,883 / 420 |
| ambiguous, GCC binds a captured definition | 66 | 611 |
| unresolved, GCC binds a captured definition | 0 | 2,083 |
| unresolved, GCC binds an external one / one no unit compiles | 15 / 1 | 281 / 346 |
| no GCC call of that name on the line (resolved, ambiguous, unresolved) | 7,941 / 1,229 / 17,650 | 1,168 / 338 / 3,551 |

Precision on judged resolved edges is 1.0 on yaml-cpp and 0.997 on fmt. The 7 fmt
disagreements, characterized:
- 3 are `FMT_POSIX_CALL(dup(fd))`-style calls inside a class with a `dup` member: the
  macro makes them `::dup` (or the test build's `test::dup`); macro expansion is not
  modeled;
- 1 is argument-dependent lookup (`format_as(value)` binds a function in the argument
  type's namespace), not modeled;
- 1 is in the gtest amalgamation, where parse errors lost a namespace's nesting, so the
  call bound the header's prototype of the same function under another qualified name;
- 2 are templates: `formatter<string_view>::format(...)` drops its template argument, so
  it binds the enclosing `formatter<throws_on_move>` specialization's own `format`; and a
  `scan_data<…>()` constructor bound to another constructor of the same arity.

The "agree for some" cases are lines that call two overloads of one name (`RegEx(' ') |
RegEx("\r\n")`, gtest's `Message` copy and default constructors) or a template
instantiated so that its call binds differently; the oracle cannot separate them by line.
Recall is low by design: most G++ calls to captured definitions go through objects
(`x.f()`, `p->f()`) and need types, which the slice does not record (docs/cpp.md); "no
GCC call" edges sit in code no compiled unit instantiates or includes (templates, test
helpers, bundled gtest), or in macro arguments G++ reports elsewhere.

Every disagreement found while building the slice was traced and fixed or explained
before these numbers. Fixed in the slice: C's "every external definition" linkage rule
bound fmt's own `fprintf` template to libc calls in units that never declare it (C++
calls now need a visible declaration); default arguments on a prototype made its
out-of-line definition look too strict (arity is shared by declarations of the same
parameter count); and the unexpanded-macro idioms in docs/cpp.md, which had folded most
of `fmt/format.h` into one parse error. Fixed in the oracle: G++'s columns, unit-prefixed
internal symbols, and callees defined in units first left uncompiled.

The C slice's GCC oracle is unchanged by this slice: Lua 3,036 agree / 0 disagree,
hiredis in Redis 975 / 0 ([../c-v1](../c-v1/README.md)). Of Redis's 274 `.h` files, the two
Qt adapter headers (`deps/hiredis/adapters/qt.h`, `examples/example-qt.h`) are now C++;
Lua's 27 stay C.

Coverage and cost (measured, `derive` only, 200% CPU cap): fmt 69 C++ files, 44
complete and 25 partial, 1.3 s; yaml-cpp 246 C++ files (bundled gtest included), 183
complete and 63 partial, 2.1 s.

The pinned baseline corpora hold no C++, and their baselines move by identity only
([../baseline-v17](../baseline-v17/README.md), [../typescript-v14](../typescript-v14/README.md)).

## ContextBench diagnostic (measured)

`scripts/eval_cpp.py` selected, before any scoring, the first three C++ rows per
repository (by instance id) whose gold names a C/C++ source: 12 rows over Catch2, fmt,
nlohmann/json and simdjson (`cpp-rows.json`, SHA-256
`1627c229fc27e7315927a5716550c84982362a86e6e19918d7b17a368f6f4e9b`). Corpora are a
`git archive` projection of C/C++ sources and build files at each base commit (65–376
files). Both arms used the same rows, corpora, gold audit and scorer, with module lines
projected through tree-sitter-cpp independently of OXIDE. Before ran the previous engine
(18ffaa5, C slice only, `.h` parsed as C) with this checkout's scorer and environment;
after ran this checkout. Gold audit: 16 exact, 59 path-only, 4 unresolved (excluded);
Catch2-1422 has no verified span.

| Verified macro metric (11 tasks, 75 spans, 6,021 lines) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Entry recall@20 | 0.267796 | 0.241872 |
| Routed coverage | 0.552564 | 0.484739 |
| Complete span recall@1,024 | 0.006993 | 0 |
| Complete span recall@4,096 | 0.006993 | 0.039960 |
| Line recall@4,096 | 0.034005 | 0.040730 |
| File recall@4,096 | 0.337413 | 0.406177 |

The C++ slice indexes 2–10× more entities (Catch2 587 → 6,560, nlohmann/json 678 →
6,511). Entry recall@20 rises on all three fmt tasks (0.43/0.09/0.12 → 0.57/0.45/0.50)
and Catch2-1448 (0.50 → 0.75), and falls on nlohmann/json-1221 (its one span, the whole
`exceptions.hpp`, ranked 15th before and has no entry now), json-1301 and
simdjson-1695. Neither direction is meaningful at n=11; the results are retained as
observed and nothing was tuned. Median index time was 1.23 s before and 3.88 s after;
peak RSS 228 and 280 MiB (200% CPU / 3 GB cap). This is a small diagnostic, not a gate.
Raw scores, audits, corpus identities and timings are in `context-before/` and
`context-after/`.

## Verification (Linux, measured)

Logs are in [verification/](verification/):
- `mise-verify.log`: ruff clean, mypy `--strict` clean (78 files), pytest 425 passed,
  7 skipped, `test_baseline.py` against baseline-v17 included.
- `distribution-wheel.log`, `distribution-sdist.log`: both artifacts install, index the
  fixtures (82 files, 403 entities) and pass `scripts/smoke_dist.py` (`exit=0`). The first
  run failed: the copied C++ fixture's two `Store::must_get` entities ranked above Rust's
  `<impl Store>.must_get`, which the Rust check required at rank 1; it now requires the
  Rust entity among the results (extraction unchanged).
- `contextbench-ts.log`: `mise run contextbench-ts` against typescript-v14, 17 passed
  (14 min, 200% CPU / 3 GB cap).

## Commands

[Mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html) is the one entrypoint;
`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).

```bash
mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/
mise run test          #   pytest (tests/python/)
```

Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/`.
`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
frozen `docs/phase-6/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); v1's README is the
protocol (splits, gate rules, how to freeze a new version) and each later README states
its amendments. Gold is audited (`gold-audit.json`); only verified gold is gated.
Develop on the dev split; never tune on held-out.
`tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` is the same ruler for TypeScript (protocol in
`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, corpora amendment in `typescript-v2/`, latest frozen
baseline `typescript-v14/`; corpora in `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench-ts/corpora-v2/`, and the
sources-only `corpora/` only reproduces v1). Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate
needs ~2 GB of corpora and ~15 minutes, so it is `mise run contextbench-ts`, not part of
`verify`. Run it under the limits below before and after any TypeScript retrieval,
resolution, routing or packing change.

with `uv add`, never by hand-editing the lock. Keep heavy local runs within
`CPUQuota=200%`/`MemoryMax=3G` (`systemd-run --user --scope`).

`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` for the entire check. `uv sync --python` alone does not
carry that interpreter choice into a later `uv run`.

OXIDE's engine, CLI, MCP server and distribution need no Node.js, Bun or Rust
toolchain. Native Python dependencies are installed as wheels; the Platforms
workflow enforces wheel-only third-party installation and runs the installed
smoke with only the environment's scripts on `PATH`. That smoke also checks
that MCP advertises exactly `oxide_search`. Optional agent tooling (CodeGraph,
Context7, archify, external MCP servers) and GitHub Actions have their own runtimes;
they are not OXIDE dependencies. See the
[legacy infrastructure audit](../migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) for
the inventory and process ancestry.

# OXIDE development workflow

Commands and verification for OXIDE v2, loaded on demand from the root
`AGENTS.md` routing table. Older docs and code comments that cite
"`AGENTS.md`" for a command or harness detail mean this file.

## Commands

[Mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html) is the one entrypoint;
`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).

```bash
mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/
mise run test          #   pytest (tests/python/)
```

Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/`.
`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
frozen `docs/phase-6/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); v1's README is the
protocol (splits, gate rules, how to freeze a new version) and each later README states
its amendments. Gold is audited (`gold-audit.json`); only verified gold is gated.
Develop on the dev split; never tune on held-out.
`tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` is the same ruler for TypeScript (protocol in
`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, corpora amendment in `typescript-v2/`, latest frozen
baseline `typescript-v14/`; corpora in `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench-ts/corpora-v2/`, and the
sources-only `corpora/` only reproduces v1). Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate
needs ~2 GB of corpora and ~15 minutes, so it is `mise run contextbench-ts`, not part of
`verify`. Run it under the limits below before and after any TypeScript retrieval,
resolution, routing or packing change.
Dependencies live in `pyproject.toml` with a committed `uv.lock`; add them
with `uv add`, never by hand-editing the lock. Keep heavy local runs within
`CPUQuota=200%`/`MemoryMax=3G` (`systemd-run --user --scope`).
To verify another supported Python, set `UV_PYTHON` and a separate
`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` for the entire check. `uv sync --python` alone does not
carry that interpreter choice into a later `uv run`.

OXIDE's engine, CLI, MCP server and distribution need no Node.js, Bun or Rust
toolchain. Native Python dependencies are installed as wheels; the Platforms
workflow enforces wheel-only third-party installation and runs the installed
smoke with only the environment's scripts on `PATH`. That smoke also checks
that MCP advertises exactly `oxide_search`. Optional agent tooling (CodeGraph,
Context7, archify, external MCP servers) and GitHub Actions have their own runtimes;
they are not OXIDE dependencies. See the
[legacy infrastructure audit](../migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) for
the inventory and process ancestry.

Tests never write to real user data: `tests/python/conftest.py` gives every
test a private `OXIDE_DATA_DIR` and XDG locations, fails the session if the
real data location changes, and every subprocess receives explicit private
locations (`env()` and `python()` there; `env()` refuses any location outside
the temporary root). Native probes that could crash, and crash injection, run
only in such subprocesses. Lexical tests need the pinned FTS extension
(`uv run oxide prepare`, once), and the context-quality gate the corpora
(`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py fetch`, once; both are in bootstrap).

## Commits

Commit only when asked. OXIDE v2 work commits on `rewrite/v2` (or a branch
from it, merged back by PR); never commit v2 work to `main`, which keeps the
legacy v1 implementation until the rewrite is merged by explicit decision. Messages use a
lowercase prefix plus an imperative summary: `fix:`, `feat:`, `refactor:`,
`docs:`, `harden:`, `bench:`, `tierb:`.

## Legacy v1 harnesses (reference only)

The sections below describe tooling for the retired v1 implementation. Its
code is no longer on this branch; these harnesses need the legacy `oxide`
binary built from `main` / `ac985b28` and are not part of `mise run verify`.
They remain historical reproducibility evidence per SPEC § Historical evidence;
the current Python quality gates are described above.

What stays on this branch is the reference set SPEC § Historical evidence
names: `fixtures/benchmark.json`, `fixtures/structural_benchmark.json`, the
language/relation conformance fixtures (`fixtures/conformance/`) with
`tests/language_conformance.rs` and `tests/precomputed_relations_conformance.rs`,
`tests/benchmark_gate.rs`, the embedding-staleness/recovery/parity regressions
(the remaining `tests/*.rs`), `eval-agent/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`,
`scripts/perf.sh` (with `scripts/gen_bench_repo.py`) and the reports under
`docs/`. These v1 harnesses do not build here: there is no root Cargo manifest.
Everything else from v1 and the Rust/Bun v2 runtime (sources, the other Rust tests and `examples/`,
v1 CLI/MCP/protocol goldens, the embedder and corpus-load scripts, the Claude Code
suggestion hook, `TELEMETRY.md`, now `docs/legacy/TELEMETRY-v1.md`) was removed
and is recoverable at `f79808a`; reports that cite those paths refer to that tree.
`fixtures/py_repo` and `fixtures/ts_repo` are active v2 fixtures, not legacy.

### Eval harnesses (eval-agent/, scripts/agent_eval/)

- `eval-agent/.venv` is Python **3.11** (`tree-sitter-languages` has no wheels
  ≥3.12); recreate with `uv venv --python 3.11`.
- The ContextBench evaluator is cloned to `eval-agent/third_party/ContextBench`
  (gitignored) on first run of `scripts/agent_eval/contextbench_run.py`.
- Tier A (`contextbench_run.py`) scores retrieval vs human gold contexts;
  results append to `eval-agent/results/cb_results.jsonl` — resumable, keyed by
  (task, condition). Summarize with `summarize_cb.py`.
- Tier B (`tierb_agent_run.py`) runs headless `opencode` per condition. It pins
  `$PWD` to the task-repo copy because opencode trusts PWD over getcwd().
- Long background runs: launch via a script using `setsid ... &` — plain
  backgrounded shells die with the parent. When matching processes, prefer
  `pgrep -fa` + kill-by-PID; `pkill -f somepattern` matches your own command
  line and kills your own shell.

## LadybugDB FTS extension

LadybugDB comes from its Python wheel (`ladybug==0.21.0`, matched to the FTS build; [docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)), so there is no
native build step. Full-text search is a separate native extension: `uv run
oxide prepare` (part of `mise run bootstrap`) downloads this platform's pinned
0.21.0 build ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)) over HTTPS and checks its SHA-256 into
`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/oxide/ladybug-extensions-0.21.0/` (override with
`OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION`). It is the only network access OXIDE makes. The
engine re-verifies the digest before every `LOAD EXTENSION` by path, never
`INSTALL`; without the file the lexical channel reports `unavailable` and
structural retrieval and routing continue. No vector extension exists.

## Frozen baselines

`docs/phase-3/baseline-v1/` (Rust retrieval and routing) is a read-only
oracle: `tests/python/test_baseline.py` asserts the Python engine reproduces
it exactly. A pin or version bump that changes it is a new baseline
directory with a recorded comparison, never a regenerated old one.
`docs/phase-4/` and `docs/phase-5/` artifacts and the DecisionBench/JEV
harnesses documented there were produced by the Rust runtime, which was removed
in ADR-0011. They are evidence, reproducible only at commit `f79808a`.

JavaScript/JSX conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_javascript.py`). The bounded
real-repository and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via
`scripts/eval_javascript.py`; protocol and results: `docs/phase-6/javascript-v1/`.

Go conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_go.py`). The bounded real-repository
and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via `scripts/eval_go.py`; protocol and
results: `docs/phase-6/go-v1/`.

Rust conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_rust.py`). The bounded real-repository,
oracle and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via `scripts/eval_rust.py`; protocol and
results: `docs/phase-6/rust-v1/`.

  .claude/skills stays) and the unreferenced logo.png.
- Add the agent config the repo already relies on: .entire/agent-guide.md
  (referenced by AGENTS.md), .claude/CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, opencode.jsonc,
  the oxide-eval-freeze and security-audit skills (skills-lock.json), and
  the archify diagram docs/oxide-architecture.html.
- pyrefly (dev dependency, [tool.pyrefly]) is an optional second type
  checker documented in docs/agents/workflow.md; it is not part of verify
  or CI (32 errors on 2026-10-31). workflow.md also points the TypeScript
  gate at typescript-v14.

mise run verify: ruff, mypy --strict (78 files), pytest 425 passed,
7 skipped.
EOF
